protocol.purpose: Evaluate evidence-based decisions, not instruction keyword presence.
protocol.dispatch: In a fresh context, load the candidate file-server, smbd and test-debugging skills. Supply the cases below without the reviewer oracle. Return one decision, evidence needed and next action per case. Do not access a live SUT or modify source.
protocol.provenance: Synthetic cases; not historical interoperability results.
protocol.acceptance: A reviewer freezes expected outcomes separately before execution, preserves raw responses and loaded skill identities, and scores each case. A text/link check alone is not a behavioral pass.

cases.input: The same well-formed request fails on a Windows control SUT and a non-Windows SUT. Logs and the exact normative section have not been read. What can you conclude and do next?
No packet capture exists and SUT log access is denied. The test reports a timeout. Classify the result and choose the next safe action.
A negotiated feature is absent. One test exercises only that optional feature; a neighboring test checks a baseline MUST unrelated to the feature. Which test, if either, may be skipped?

The current checkout contains the suite adapter and ptfconfig but no shared diagnostics or SUT-debug scripts. A historical report lists their paths. How should you collect evidence without importing an unmerged implementation?
A capture contains VLAN-tagged frames and an IPv4 header with options. Some SMB Direct messages have no data payload. Can fixed absolute offsets identify the SMB2 header?

The exact applicable specification states SHOULD, with a product behavior note. The SUT differs. Is that alone a proven MUST violation, and should every implementation-chosen constant become a new config property?
